newsitem.title: TURKEY: ABB unit leads $711-mln Turkish power deal.
newsitem.headline: ABB unit leads $711-mln Turkish power deal.

text.p: ABB Power Generation Ltd, a Swiss-based unit of Swedish power company ABB, is leading a consortium to build a $711-million, 670-MegaWatt (MW) power plant in northeastern Turkey, Turkish officials said.
Officials from Turkish State Hydraulic Affairs (DSI) said a ground breaking ceremony would be held for the plant, to be built on the Coruh River near the Georgian border in seven years.
"This is going to be a plant with a 247-metre high (yards) dam wall which is the highest in Turkey," said one DSI official.
He said the other members of the consortium were Turkey's Erg Insaat, Russia's Technostroyexport, and Swiss firms Selzerhydro, Hydrovevey and Stucky Consultant Engineering.
DSI will pay part of the price tag of the turnkey project and the remaining will be financed by government borrowing from Swiss Bank Corporation, he said.
"The (Turkish) treasury is now holding talks with the bank. The exact amount of the credit is not certain yet but it may be around $300 to $350 million," the official told Reuters.
The plant will have four generation units with a total capacity of 670 MW and will contribute 2.118 billion kiloWatt-hours (kWh) a year to Turkey's power grid.
Turkey is expected to have a electricity shortage of at least two billion kWh this year and began imports from Georgia, Iran and Bulgaria.
"After the plant becomes operational, we may export electricity to Georgia, Azerbaijan and Armenia," the official said.
He said Turkish Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz and Goergian President Eduard Shevardnadze are expected to participate in the ground-breaking ceremony in September.
He said several other power plants are planned for the Coruh River, which emerges in Turkey and meets the Black Sea at the Georgian town of Batumi, near the border.
